title: Product Catalog and Knowledge Graph
card: Compatibility coverage across the catalog raised from 57% to 99.6% of products.
what: I built the layer that turns the ERP's product model into what the public website shows, and the knowledge graph that answers which parts work together.
problem: The ERP stores option names as raw internal strings and versions a product by duplicating its record, so nothing in it is shaped like a product page. Customers also ask which accessory fits which unit, and that answer lived in support articles and in the heads of the people who have been there longest.
result: The website renders from a model covering more than 56 product types, and compatibility coverage went from 57% of products to 99.6%.
how: Five services read the product model out of PostgreSQL and emit what the storefront expects, with raw option names mapped into categories a customer can actually read. A product page composes from nine independent fragments in roughly 300ms, and each fragment is isolated, so one slow section degrades itself and not the page.

The knowledge system models a sellable product as a graph, so an option a customer picks resolves into the component SKUs that choice actually adds. Spec values are harvested from support articles and every value keeps a pointer back to the article it came from, so a reviewer can check a number against its source. Each product declares its connector interfaces, and compatibility is computed from those declarations across 491 derived relationships.
